data.narrative:
Lace Lithography is a Series A-stage semiconductor company founded by Bodil Holst and Adria Salvador Palau that has raised $60M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 11 private and public peers in Chips & Semiconductors, including public companies ALAB, NVDA, and AMD alongside private companies including SambaNova Systems, Cerebras, and PsiQuantum.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable approach. Using the $60M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage progression, the method yields $120M. A peer-median approach could not be reliably deployed due to insufficient datapoints within narrow stage and valuation-tier filters; only one same-stage and one adjacent-stage peer were identified in the existing dataset, below the three-datapoint threshold needed for robust median calculation. Broadening to all 11 sector peers would introduce excessive heterogeneity and is accordingly not recommended.

The triangulated valuation range spans $102M (low) to $138M (high), with $120M as the point estimate. This range reflects a single-method derivation, which inherently carries higher uncertainty than multi-method triangulation. Key risks include the stage-multiplier assumption and the absence of narrower peer validation. Refining the estimate would benefit from closer stage-matched comparables or additional company-specific cash-burn and runway data.
